title: Scene × chunk factorization of video Mirror roles
hypothesis: A shared HNeRV decoder with scene-factor × temporal-chunk coordinates can represent held-out scene-window combinations more compactly than a flat chunk/embedding table without losing frame PSNR, scene-cut fidelity or decode FPS.
physical_object: HNeRV content-adaptive video encoder and common image decoder.
mirror_coordinate: Factorized scene identity × temporal chunk role.
logical_multiplicity: Scene-window combinations decoded from a shared neural video object.

development.selection_metric: Not run; upstream provides a single Bunny video only.

storage.authority: actual serialized decoder plus embedding/code payload bytes

success_gate: Not evaluated; requires held-out scene×window combinations and real frame reconstruction/bitstream/decode measurement.
blockers: Official HNeRV upstream has a single 132-frame Bunny video/checkpoint, not multiple fitted scenes or scene-window pairs.
NerVast implementation/checkpoints/Fisher masks remain unavailable; CUDA/NVIDIA is unavailable for the registered native-comparator rate-distortion and FPS run.
boundaries: CPU smoke confirms only one-video HNeRV decode; it is not scene×chunk experiment evidence.
Do not treat Bunny temporal windows as independent scenes.
No synthetic proxy or single-scene substitute is used.
